components.name: Glass Tile over Circuit Grid
components.description: Signature material: flat at rest; on hover (standing in for scroll) the dotted teal grid fades in and the tile frosts it. No border, no shadow.

components.css: .ds-board { position: relative; padding: 48px; background-color: #111418; color: #e8e8e8; font: 400 16px/1.5 Lato, sans-serif; } .ds-board::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0; opacity: 0; background-image: linear-gradient(90deg, #61B3AF 1px, transparent 1px), linear-gradient(0deg, #61B3AF 1px, transparent 1px); background-size: 32px 32px; -webkit-mask: repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, #000 0 1px, transparent 1px 3px); mask: repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, #000 0 1px, transparent 1px 3px); transition: opacity 750ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); } .ds-tile { position: relative; padding: 24px; border-radius: 4px; background: transparent; transition: background-color 750ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), backdrop-filter 750ms cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1); } .ds-tile p { margin: 8px 0 0; color: #b8c0cc; } .ds-board:hover::before { opacity: 0.14; transition-duration: 200ms; } .ds-board:hover .ds-tile { background: rgba(17, 20, 24, 0.55); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(12px); backdrop-filter: blur(12px); transition-duration: 200ms; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-board:hover::before { opacity: 0; } .ds-board:hover .ds-tile { background: transparent; backdrop-filter: none; } }

narrative.overview:
The site is a circuit board at rest. Nothing glows. Nothing floats. The reader sees a plain dark field, light text, and one teal accent. When the reader scrolls, current flows: a fine dotted grid of teal traces fades in, and the work sits on panes of soft glass above it. When the scroll stops, the current drains away and the board goes flat again.

The effect is proof of craft, not decoration. It appears only in answer to the reader's own motion, so it never competes with the content at rest. Density is low. Moves are few and strong. Every surface earns its depth by responding to something.

This is not an editorial cream-and-serif site, a Dribbble shot wall, or a bento template. The glass tiles never form a grid of boxes.
keyCharacteristics: Flat dark rest state; depth exists only in motion.
One accent (teal) that carries links, calls to action, focus, and the grid traces.
Lato everywhere, in two weights, with a tight, bold heading voice.
Hairline borders and small radii; no drop shadows.

rules.name: The One Current Rule
rules.body: Teal is the only hue. The grid, the links, and the CTAs share it. Do not add a second accent for the motion layer.

rules.name: The Flat At Rest Rule
rules.body: If the reader is not scrolling or hovering a row, the page is flat. No grid, glass, or shadow may persist at rest, and none may appear on load.

rules.name: The No Card Wall Rule
rules.body: Glass tiles have no border, no shadow, and no visible fill at rest. Only the blurred grid and the transient specular edge define their edge. At least one grid cell (16px) of sharp grid must show between neighboring tiles. If a screenshot of the Scroll state reads as a bento or a wall of cards, the tile is too strong: lower the tint or blur, never add an edge.

rules.name: The Still Reader Rule
rules.body: Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, the page stays in Rest. The grid and glass never appear.

dos: **Do** keep the page flat Board Ink at rest and on load.
**Do** tie the grid and glass to scroll activity only, and decay them together over 750ms.
**Do** keep the grid fixed to the viewport, on a 16px pitch, in teal at 0.14 peak opacity.
**Do** keep tile geometry identical across states so nothing moves when the material changes.
**Do** honor reduced motion by staying in Rest.
donts: **Don't** give glass tiles a border, shadow, or resting fill. That makes a card wall.
**Don't** arrange tiles into a bento or a dense box grid.
**Don't** add a second accent color for the grid or glass.
**Don't** use drop shadows anywhere for depth.
**Don't** let the grid, blur, or tint hold after scrolling stops.
